sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: Well, it's Christmas Day, of course.
It's Christmas Day, and we're celebrating with two fun stories from The Illusionist,
sentences.zh: 今天是圣诞节，我们将通过海伦·扎尔茨曼的节目《幻术师》中的两个有趣故事来庆祝，

sentences.en: a show about language from Helen Zaltzman.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于语言的节目，由海伦·扎尔茨曼主持。

sentences.en: The Illusionist is one of my all-time favorite podcasts,
sentences.zh: 《幻术师》是我有史以来最喜欢的播客之一，

sentences.en: and I'm not just saying that because Helen Zaltzman is one of my all-time favorite people.
sentences.zh: 我这么说可不仅仅是因为海伦·扎尔茨曼是我最喜欢的人之一。

sentences.en: It is a show about language, but it is absolutely not just for word nerds.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于语言的节目，但绝对不仅仅是写给字词书呆子看的。

sentences.en: It is 99PI-style storytelling using language as the lens to view culture rather than design.
sentences.zh: 它是99PI风格的叙事，以语言为镜头来观察文化而非设计。

sentences.en: And if you haven't discovered it yet, you are going to love it.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没发现它，你一定会爱上它。

sentences.en: With two festive seasonal favorites from The Illusionist, here's Helen Zaltzman.
sentences.zh: 借着《幻术师》中两个充满节日气氛的最爱，接下来请听海伦·扎尔茨曼的讲述。

sentences.en: Upon the birth of Jesus Christ himself, when King Herod ordered all the baby boys in and around Bethlehem be killed.
sentences.zh: 早在耶稣基督诞生时，希律王下令杀害伯利恒及周边地区所有的小男孩。

sentences.en: In 1644, when Oliver Cromwell's Puritans passed an ordinance prohibiting Christmas celebrations in England.
sentences.zh: 在1644年，奥利弗·克伦威尔的清教徒通过了一项法令，禁止在英国庆祝圣诞节。

sentences.en: In 1659, when the Massachusetts Bay Colony Puritans managed to get Christmas banned for 22 years for being a pagan festival.
sentences.zh: 在1659年，马萨诸塞湾殖民地的清教徒成功让圣诞节被禁22年，理由它是异教节日。

sentences.en: Or was it in 1998, in Britain's second largest city, Birmingham?
sentences.zh: 还是在1998年，在英国第二大城市伯明翰？

sentences.en: If you picked up practically any newspaper at the time,
sentences.zh: 如果你当时随便拿起一张报纸，

sentences.en: you would have read that Birmingham City Council had renamed Christmas Winterval.
sentences.zh: 你就会读到伯明翰市议会将圣诞节重新命名为“冬日节”（Winterval）。

sentences.en: Birmingham will celebrate the festive season as usual this year with carol singing, fairy lights and street entertainment.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰今年将一如既往地庆祝节日季，有唱赞美诗、仙女灯和街头娱乐。

sentences.en: Council officials have renamed it Winterval in the hope of creating a more multicultural atmosphere
sentences.zh: 市议会官员将其改名为“冬日节”，希望营造出更多元的文化氛围，

sentences.en: in keeping with the city's mix of ethnic groups.
sentences.zh: 以契合这座城市多元的族群融合。

sentences.en: A politically correct decision to call Christmas festivities Winterval.
sentences.zh: 这是一个将圣诞庆祝活动命名为“冬日节”的政治正确决定。
市议会的圣诞节，叫它“冬日节”。

sentences.en: Birmingham Council, claiming it was anxious not to offend those in other faiths, renamed Christmas Winterval.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰市议会声称急于不冒犯其他信仰的人，因此将圣诞节改名为“冬日节”。

sentences.en: Crazy council chiefs provoked outrage last night after naming Christmas festivities Winterval.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的市议会负责人昨晚因将圣诞节庆祝活动命名为“冬日节”而引发众怒。

sentences.en: Churchmen believe the Winterval name is intended to avoid offending Muslims and other minorities.
sentences.zh: 神职人员认为“冬日节”这个名字旨在避免冒犯穆斯林和其他少数群体。

sentences.en: A municipal brainwave called Winterval, renaming the annual holiday and likening it to shopping rather than shepherds.
sentences.zh: 一个名为“冬日节”的市政灵光一闪，将年度节日重新命名，并将其比作购物而非牧羊人。

sentences.en: The word Winterval has a nasty echo of communists who banned any Christian connotation in East Germany.
sentences.zh: “冬日节”这个词有着讨厌的共产主义者的回响，他们在东德禁止任何基督教色彩。

sentences.en: And verily, in Britain, Christmas was banished.
sentences.zh: 而且确实，在英国，圣诞节被放逐了。

sentences.en: Now we sing Winterval carols and wear ironic Winterval sweaters.
sentences.zh: 现在我们唱着“冬日节”赞美诗，穿着讽刺性的“冬日节”毛衣。

sentences.en: We hang up our Winterval stockings for Father Winterval to fill with Winterval gifts.
sentences.zh: 我们挂起“冬日节”长筒袜，等待“冬日节老人”塞满“冬日节”礼物。

sentences.en: And when we turn on the radio, we rock around the Winterval tree to these festive tunes.
sentences.zh: 当打开收音机时，我们伴随着这些节日曲调绕着“冬日节”树摇摆。

sentences.en: May be all I want for Winterval.
sentences.zh: 可能是我对“冬日节”的全部渴望。
没错，事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: Well, it's about as true as most things that have been said about Winterval, which came about thanks to one Mike Chubb.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它和关于“冬日节”的大多数言论一样真实，而这一切都要归功于一个叫迈克·查布的人。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Mike Chubb.
You could say that I was the one that has caused a fury that is Winterval.
sentences.zh: 你可以说我就是引发“冬日节”这场狂怒的人。

sentences.en: In the late 1990s, Mike Chubb was the head of events for Birmingham City Council.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代末，迈克·查布是伯明翰市议会的活动主管。

sentences.en: From our point of view, from myself as the manager of this huge events section in Birmingham City Council, and my team of some like 30, we came up with the terminology Winterval.
sentences.zh: 从我们的角度来看，作为伯明翰市议会这个庞大活动部门的经理，我和我大约30人的团队，我们想出了“冬日节”这个术语。

sentences.en: It's like a portmanteau word for winter and festival.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一个由冬天（winter）和节日（festival）组合而成的混成词。

sentences.en: I thought it was a portmanteau of winter and interval, I must say, to sort of suggest this hiatus in the year.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我原以为它是冬天（winter）和间歇（interval）的混成词，用来暗示一年中的这段间歇期。

sentences.en: No, it's between winter and festival.
sentences.zh: 不，它介于冬天和节日之间。

sentences.en: I think it's a good portmanteau.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很好的混成词。

sentences.en: Until it became shorthand for war on Christmas with a side of political correctness gone mad.
sentences.zh: 直到它成了“向圣诞宣战”并附赠“政治正确走火入魔”的代名词。

sentences.en: It started well enough with Birmingham's first Winterval in 1997.
sentences.zh: 它起步很顺利，伯明翰于1997年举办了首届“冬日节”。

sentences.en: Events ran over several weeks and were attended by hundreds of thousands of people without complaints from the press or the populace.
sentences.zh: 活动持续了几个星期，数十万人参加，没有遭到媒体或民众的投诉。

sentences.en: So it's not clear why the following year's Winterval became a wincident.
sentences.zh: 所以目前尚不清楚为什么第二年的“冬日节”会变成一场“赢灾”（wincident）。

sentences.en: In November 1998, the then Bishop of Birmingham, Mark Santa, no, not as in Claus, issued his Christmas message to the clergy of the diocese.
sentences.zh: 1998年11月，时任伯明翰主教马克·圣塔（不，不是圣诞老人Claus），向教区神职人员发布了圣诞致辞。

sentences.en: And soon, the papers got hold of it.
sentences.zh: 很快，报纸就抓住不放了。

sentences.en: On the 8th of November 1998, the Birmingham Sunday Mercury reported that the Bishop of Birmingham had condemned the City Council's attempt to rebrand Christmas.
sentences.zh: 1998年11月8日，伯明翰《星期日水星报》报道称，伯明翰主教谴责了市议会重塑圣诞节的企图。

sentences.en: What happened then was, of course, all those papers.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情当然就是所有这些报纸都在说，

sentences.en: Hey, this is a good week, you know, not much news at Christmas, is there?
sentences.zh: 嘿，这是个不错的一周，你知道的，圣诞节期间没什么新闻，对吧？
让我们用一个有趣的故事。

sentences.en: Did you know Birmingham City Council of Council Christmas or renamed Christmas Winterval?
sentences.zh: 你知道伯明翰市议会关于市议会圣诞节或者将圣诞节重新命名为“冬日节”的事吗？

sentences.en: Thereafter, it went nationwide and worldwide.
sentences.zh: 此后，它传遍了全国乃至全球。

sentences.en: Pretty much the only person who didn't notice was Mike Chubb.
sentences.zh: 几乎唯一没有注意到的人就是迈克·查布。

sentences.en: I was so busy at the time.
I didn't take in any of the media furore at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时根本没有理会任何媒体的狂热。

sentences.en: It just didn't touch me at all, because I literally, we were working 41 days non-stop, day and night.
sentences.zh: 它根本没有触动我，因为说实话，我们当时连续工作了41天，日夜不停。

sentences.en: Busy work waging the war on Christmas, except that wasn't really what Mike and the Council were doing during the war on the war on Christmas.
sentences.zh: 忙着进行向圣诞宣战的战争，不过这其实并不是迈克和市议会在反圣诞之战期间所做的事情。

sentences.en: In this war, only one side turned up to the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 在这场战争中，只有一方来到了战场。

sentences.en: It was the media, really, that actually took it on.
sentences.zh: 实际上是媒体把这件事挑起来的。

sentences.en: People like the Daily Mail, just go on to Google and Google Winterval and just look at the organisations who are up in arms about it.
sentences.zh: 像《每日邮报》这样的人，只要去谷歌搜索“冬日节”，看看那些对此气愤填膺的机构就知道了。

sentences.en: They're up in arms because they've been led to believe that that's what Birmingham City Council intended.
sentences.zh: 他们气愤是因为他们被误导，以为这就是伯明翰市议会的意图。

sentences.en: Christmas was never off the page.
sentences.zh: 圣诞节从来没有从页面上消失过。

sentences.en: It was part of a 41-day, if you like, festival of events.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，它是一场为期41天的活动节的一部分。

sentences.en: But people thought you were trying to rebrand Christmas.
sentences.zh: 但人们以为你们在试图重塑圣诞节。

sentences.en: They said it's political correctness gone mad.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是政治正确走火入魔。

sentences.en: But actually, political correctness had not gone mad.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，政治正确并没有走火入魔。

sentences.en: Political correctness had not even been a factor.
sentences.zh: 政治正确甚至都不是一个因素。

sentences.en: Because the Council's events team was not trying to rebrand Christmas.
sentences.zh: 因为市议会的活动团队并不是在试图重塑圣诞节。

sentences.en: It was trying to bundle together a whole lot of events occurring in the weeks before and after Christmas.
sentences.zh: 它是在试图将圣诞节前后几周内发生的一大堆活动捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: Birmingham is Britain's second largest city, with a very culturally and ethnically diverse population.
sentences.zh: 伯明翰是英国第二大城市，拥有非常多元的文化和族群人口。

sentences.en: There's a lot of stuff going on, particularly at that time of year.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情正在发生，特别是在一年中的那个时候。

sentences.en: Hence, they decided to use the marketing banner Winterval.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们决定使用“冬日节”这个营销横幅。

sentences.en: You feel like it does what it says on the tin.
sentences.zh: 你觉得它做到了名副其实。

sentences.en: It markets a major festival at a time of the year called Winter.
sentences.zh: 它在一年中被称为冬天的时期推广一个重大节日。

sentences.en: And there are all sorts of things that happen in Winter.
sentences.zh: 冬天会发生各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: You know, Diwali happens in Winter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，排灯节发生在冬天。

sentences.en: BBC Children in Need happens in Winter.
sentences.zh: BBC儿童慈善义演发生在冬天。

sentences.en: You know, Chinese New Year happens in Winter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，中国农历新年发生在冬天。

sentences.en: New Year's Eve happens in Winter.
That particular event, which included the Christmas lights switch on,
sentences.zh: 那个特定的活动，包括亮灯仪式，

sentences.en: it was about a month of events over Christmas.
sentences.zh: 那是圣诞节期间大约一个月的活动。

sentences.en: It had its own brochure, Christmas.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的宣传册，圣诞节。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, people decided not to see that.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，人们选择看不到这一点。

sentences.en: They decided that that's what the Council did.
sentences.zh: 他们认定市议会就是这么干的。

sentences.en: Shortly after the war on Winterval erupted in the papers,
sentences.zh: 在报纸上爆发“冬日节之战”后不久，

sentences.en: the Council actually issued a statement that they were not renaming Christmas,
sentences.zh: 市议会实际上发表了一份声明，表示他们没有给圣诞节改名，

sentences.en: and Christmas was very visibly a major part of the Winterval line-up.
sentences.zh: 而且圣诞节非常明显地是“冬日节”阵容中的重要部分。
但哪个故事更深入人心？

sentences.en: The true one, that Winterval was a marketing and admin umbrella,
sentences.zh: 真实的故事，即“冬日节”是一个营销和管理的保护伞，

sentences.en: or the lie that Winterval had come to kill Christmas?
sentences.zh: 还是谎言说“冬日节”是为了杀死圣诞节？

sentences.en: Now, personally, I've noticed significantly more uproar about the war on Christmas
sentences.zh: 现在，就我个人而言，我注意到关于反圣诞之战的喧嚣明显要多得多，

sentences.en: than actual evidence that that war is being waged.
sentences.zh: 而这场战争正在进行的实际证据却很少。

sentences.en: Some people seem very eager for there to be a war on Christmas so they can leap to Christmas's defence.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎非常渴望有一场反圣诞之战，这样他们就可以跳出来捍卫圣诞节。

sentences.en: Though Christmas has achieved cultural dominance way beyond religious lines,
sentences.zh: 尽管圣诞节已经取得了超越宗教界限的文化主导地位，

sentences.en: to cast it as an underdog provides a cover for taking a pop at other cultures,
sentences.zh: 将其塑造成弱势群体，实际上是为攻击其他文化提供了掩护，

sentences.en: and to create and maintain divisions in society.
sentences.zh: 并在社会中制造和维持分裂。

sentences.en: But Christmas is a pagan Roman Christian festival,
sentences.zh: 但圣诞节是一个异教的、罗马的、基督教的节日，

sentences.en: celebrated by people from all sorts of cultures with all sorts of beliefs,
sentences.zh: 由来自各种文化、有着各种信仰的人们共同庆祝，

sentences.en: including me, an ethnically Jewish atheiSt.
sentences.zh: 包括我，一个有犹太血统的无神论者。

sentences.en: Christmas is not threatened by multiculturalism.
sentences.zh: 圣诞节并没有受到多元文化的威胁。
它本身就是多元文化的。

sentences.en: Winterval was used as an example of a change that's gone too far,
sentences.zh: “冬日节”被用作改变走得太远的例子，

sentences.en: because they misread what the organisers are trying to do.
sentences.zh: 因为他们误解了组织者试图做的事情。

sentences.en: And they continued to misread it.
sentences.zh: 并且他们继续误解下去。

sentences.en: After 1998, Birmingham didn't run Winterval again.
sentences.zh: 1998年之后，伯明翰再也没有办过冬季欢庆节。

sentences.en: the Winterval myth was repeated dozens of times in Britain's national newspapers.
sentences.zh: 英国国家级报纸上无数次重复着冬季欢庆节的谣言。

sentences.en: In fact, in 2011, after running another such piece,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在2011年刊登了另一篇此类报道后，

sentences.en: the Daily Mail had to print a retraction,
sentences.zh: 《每日邮报》不得不发表了一篇撤回声明，

sentences.en: saying that Winterval did not rename or replace Christmas.
sentences.zh: 称冬季欢庆节并没有改名或取代圣诞节。

sentences.en: Winterval had already become the byword for political correctness gone mad.
sentences.zh: 冬季欢庆节已经成了政治正确走向极端的代名词。
而且这种现象仍在继续。

sentences.en: Just a few weeks ago in the British Parliament,
sentences.zh: 就在几周前，在英国议会中，

sentences.en: Shailesh Vara, the Conservative MP for North West Cambridgeshire,
sentences.zh: 剑桥郡西北部保守党议员沙伊利什·瓦拉，

sentences.en: that minority communities should respect the views and traditions of mainstream Britain.
sentences.zh: 少数族裔社区应该尊重英国主流社会的观点和传统。

sentences.en: And that means Christmas is not Winterval
sentences.zh: 这意味着圣诞节不是冬季欢庆节，

sentences.en: and Christmas trees are not festive trees.
I do agree with my honourable friend.
sentences.zh: 我确实同意我这位尊敬的朋友的看法。

sentences.en: Well, we can all agree with him that Christmas is not Winterval,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们都同意他的看法，即圣诞节不是冬季欢庆节，
因为它从来就不是冬季欢庆节。

sentences.en: It's not, it's not certain people just decide to say what they want to say.
sentences.zh: 这可不是说某些人随心所欲想说什么就说什么。

sentences.en: Maybe they want to create a bit of a stir because it sells papers.
sentences.zh: 也许他们想煽动一点轰动效应，因为这能帮报纸大卖。

sentences.en: But in a way, as a marketing story,
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，作为一个营销故事，

sentences.en: it is very successful because the brand really clung on.
sentences.zh: 它非常成功，因为这个品牌真的深入人心了。

sentences.en: If you just called it, I don't know, Birmingham Winter Holidays,
sentences.zh: 如果你只是把它叫做，我不知道，伯明翰寒假，
对，我的意思是，完全如此。

sentences.en: It's just unfortunate that the brand had been so misinterpreted.
sentences.zh: 只可惜这个品牌被严重误解了。

sentences.en: If you had your time again, would you do it differently?
sentences.zh: 如果时光倒流，你还会做出不同的选择吗？

sentences.en: Here's what you're going to do.
You're going to go buy that prized turkey in the window
sentences.zh: 去橱窗里买下那只珍贵的火鸡，

sentences.en: and settle in for another story from The Illusionist,
sentences.zh: 然后准备收听《幻术师》的另一个故事，

sentences.en: featuring a couple of familiar 99PI voices after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后节目中将邀请几位熟悉的99PI播客声音。

sentences.en: Here again is The Illusionist on 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形节目播出的《幻术师》。

sentences.en: So we're in the parking lot of Cow Palace.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在在牛宫的停车场里。

sentences.en: There's a gun show happening at the same time.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这里正在举办一场枪械展。
上面写着：欢迎，爱国者们。

sentences.en: We are here for the Dickens FeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们是来参加狄更斯节的。

sentences.en: Katie Mingle and Avery Truffleman of 99% Invisible
sentences.zh: 99%隐形节目的凯蒂·明格尔和艾弗里·特鲁夫曼

sentences.en: are about to enter Victorian London
sentences.zh: 即将走进维多利亚时代的伦敦，

sentences.en: in the Cow Palace Arena in Daly City,
sentences.zh: 位于戴利城的牛宫竞技场，

sentences.en: just south of San Francisco, California.
sentences.zh: 就位于加利福尼亚州旧金山南部。

sentences.en: It's also, like, sunny and 60-ish degrees.
sentences.zh: 而且天气也差不多是阳光明媚，60华氏度左右。

sentences.en: It feels not Christmassy at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也没有圣诞节的感觉。

sentences.en: The Great Dickens Christmas Fair entrance.
sentences.zh: 伟大的狄更斯圣诞集市入口。

sentences.en: It's a giant portrait of Santa Claus as you walk in.
sentences.zh: 一走进去就能看到一幅巨大的圣诞老人肖像。

sentences.en: The Dickens Christmas Fair has been an annual event
